audit.recode_to: From fixed-strict initial to non-fixed / quantity-sensitive: 'stress on the syllable containing a long (or diphthongoid) vowel, otherwise on the final syllable; non-phonemic, not experimentally studied' (Novikova 1997:287, sec. 2.1.2), i.e. unbounded long-vowel-seeking with default-final, with a caution note that first-syllable short vowels are unreduced while non-first short vowels reduce (Tsintsius 1947:14; Novikova 1960 apud Aralova 2015:29-30), which is probably what the database chain read as 'initial stress'. Cite Novikova 1997 as deciding source; keep StressTyp2/Benzing as a recorded database contradiction.
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the record carries no quotation; it is a database-only coding (StressTyp2 lect 106, pattern 112 'initial', sources Benzing 1955 and Gordon 2002 with empty passage text). I confirmed the pattern-112 summary sentence and the Benzing source row in the StressTyp2 SQL dump we hold; nothing primary is held for 'initial'. (2) Deciding source: a 2015 database entry inheriting Gordon 2002's appendix label, itself resting on a 1955 German grammar nobody in our chain has opened. (3) I fetched sources two open primary descriptions. Novikova 1997 (Jazyki Mira, ILING RAN open PDF), the reference-encyclopedia chapter by the leading Even specialist, has an explicit stress paragraph (sec. 2.1.2, p. 287) stating that stress most often falls on the LAST syllable in words without long vowels and on the long/diphthongoid-vowel syllable otherwise, and is non-distinctive and experimentally unstudied. sources.quote: "2.1.2. Ударение экспериментально не исследовалось. Можно отметить, что в словах без долгих гласных оно чаще всего падает на последний слог: кума 'нерпа', мэӈэн 'деньги', куӈакан 'ребеночек', а в словах с долгим или дифтонгоидным гласным — на слог с этим гласным: моми 'лодка', туреки 'ворона', наакита 'лиственница'. Смыслоразличительного значения ударение не имеет." [Stress has not been studied experimentally. In words without long vowels it most often falls on the LAST syllable; in words with a long or diphthongoid vowel, on the syllable containing that vowel. Stress is not distinctive.]
sources.locator: sec. 2.1.2, book p. 287 (PDF p. 286; PDF page = book page - 1)

sources.quote: No word-stress section; p. 14 states only that 'normal' (short) vowels in non-first syllables are pronounced considerably shorter and with blurred articulation (a, o, e sound like an unclear ы), long vowels in non-first syllables somewhat shorter but distinct; p. 26 notes Russian stressed final vowels are borrowed as Even long vowels. Describes first-syllable vowel fullness, not stress placement.
